### AC-12 — Session Termination

**Status:** Planned · **Responsibility:** system

Not yet satisfied. Tokens carry an expiry and the maximum lifetime is capped at 30 days by configuration validation, which bounds exposure but is not termination.

> **Limitation.** There is no server-side logout and no revocation. A token remains valid until it expires, regardless of what happens to the account behind it.

### AC-3 — Access Enforcement

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** system

Every route holding user data requires a bearer token resolved by requireAuth, which sets the principal on the request context. Handlers read the authenticated user id from that context and scope all queries to it, so one account cannot reach another's entries, balance or redemptions.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/auth/middleware.ts` — Resolves and validates the principal once per request.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/routes/impact.ts` — Every query is scoped to c.get('userId').
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/__tests__/impact.test.ts` — 'keeps entries private between users' asserts cross-account isolation.

### AC-4 — Information Flow Enforcement

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** system

Cross-origin access is an explicit allowlist of exact origins. With none configured the API emits no CORS headers at all, which is the correct posture for the mobile client. Production rejects both a wildcard origin and any plaintext http origin at startup rather than at request time.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/env.ts` — parseOrigins rejects '*' and non-https origins when NODE_ENV=production.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/app.ts` — CORS middleware is only mounted when origins are configured.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/__tests__/security.test.ts` — Asserts allow-listed origins are echoed and others receive no header.

### AC-6 — Least Privilege

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** shared

The container runs as the unprivileged node user with every Linux capability dropped, no-new-privileges set, and a read-only root filesystem. CI workflows default to contents:read and widen scope only for the single job that publishes CodeQL results.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/Dockerfile` — USER node in the runtime stage.
- `evergreen:docker-compose.yml` — cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, read_only, tmpfs for /tmp.
- `evergreen:.github/workflows/security.yml` — security-events:write granted only to the codeql job.

### AC-7 — Unsuccessful Logon Attempts

**Status:** Partial · **Responsibility:** system

Credential endpoints sit behind a dedicated rate-limit bucket keyed on client address, separate from and stricter than the general API limit. Each refusal is recorded to the audit trail with the pseudonymous account id, so repeated attempts against one account are detectable.

> **Limitation.** Counters are held in process memory, so the effective limit multiplies by the replica count in a scaled deployment. There is no per-account lockout, only per-address throttling, so a distributed attempt from many addresses is slowed but not stopped.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/security/rate-limit.ts` — Fixed-window limiter behind a RateLimitStore interface.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/app.ts` — Separate buckets for /v1/auth/* and the rest of /v1/*.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/__tests__/security.test.ts` — Asserts throttling, Retry-After, and that probes are never limited.

### AU-2 — Event Logging

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** system

A closed set of security-relevant event types is emitted as structured records: registration, login success and failure, rejected tokens, rate-limit refusals, redemptions, rejected requests and startup configuration. The set is closed so detection rules can be written against stable identifiers.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/security/audit.ts` — SecurityEventType enumerates the auditable events.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts` — Records both outcomes of every authentication attempt.

### AU-3 — Content of Audit Records

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** system

Every record carries what happened, when, where, the source of the request, the outcome and the identity involved -- the six facts AU-3 requires. A correlation id is generated per request, echoed to the client and attached to each record, so a reported error can be traced to its server-side cause without exposing any detail to the caller.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/security/audit.ts` — SecurityEvent defines the required fields.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/security/context.ts` — Request id generation, validation and propagation.

### AU-9 — Protection of Audit Information

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** shared

Email addresses are hashed before they reach a log record, so repeated attempts against one account remain correlatable without writing personal data into logs that are shipped, retained and widely readable. Tokens, passwords and password hashes are never recorded. A behaviour test asserts this by scanning the emitted records for the credentials used.

> **Limitation.** Retention, access control and tamper-evidence for the shipped log stream are properties of the hosting platform's logging service, not of this code.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/security/audit.ts` — pseudonymize() hashes addresses with SHA-256.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/__tests__/security.test.ts` — 'never writes credentials or addresses into the audit trail'.

### CA-7 — Continuous Monitoring

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** system

Security gates run on every pull request and on a weekly schedule, so advisories published against unchanged code are still found. Each gate writes a machine-readable report that is retained as a build artifact and forms the evidence trail for this package.

> **Limitation.** Evidence verification is skipped in this package's own pipeline: Evergreen is private and the workflow token cannot read it, so the check that ties these controls to real files runs only locally until a read token is provisioned.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:.github/workflows/security.yml` — Scheduled weekly re-scan plus per-PR gates.
- `handoff:docs/04-continuous-monitoring.md` — Monitoring plan, frequencies and responsibilities.

### CM-2 — Baseline Configuration

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** system

The dependency tree is fixed by a committed lockfile and installed with npm ci, which fails if the lockfile and manifests disagree. The container base image is pinned by digest as well as tag, because a tag can be moved to different content.

> **Limitation.** The baseline is declared but has never been built: no container image has been produced from this Dockerfile, so the declared baseline and the real artifact have not been compared.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:package-lock.json` — Committed lockfile; npm ci is used in both build stages.
- `evergreen:apps/api/Dockerfile` — NODE_IMAGE pinned by sha256 digest.

### CM-6 — Configuration Settings

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** system

Every setting is validated at startup and the process exits 78 rather than serving traffic under an unsafe configuration. Secure values are the defaults: forwarded client addresses are not believed, no CORS origins are allowed, and request bodies are bounded.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/env.ts` — loadEnv validates and fails closed.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/__tests__/env.test.ts` — 20 tests covering the refusal paths and secure defaults.

### CM-7 — Least Functionality

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** system

The runtime image carries only the production dependency tree and compiled output: 31MB against 195MB for the build tree, with the compiler, test runner and every devDependency absent. PostgreSQL is not published to the host and is reachable only on the container network.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/Dockerfile` — Separate deps stage resolved with --omit=dev.
- `evergreen:docker-compose.yml` — No host port mapping for the database.

### CP-10 — System Recovery and Reconstitution

**Status:** Partial · **Responsibility:** shared

The service is stateless and reconstituted by redeploying the pinned image; schema state is rebuilt by re-applying the committed migrations, which are verified against an empty database on every pipeline run.

> **Limitation.** Database backup scheduling, retention and restore rehearsal belong to the hosting provider and have not been exercised. An untested restore is not a recovery capability.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:packages/db/drizzle` — Committed migrations, applied to an empty database in CI.
- `handoff:docs/07-operations-runbook.md` — Recovery procedure and its open items.

### CP-9 — System Backup

**Status:** Inherited · **Responsibility:** provider

Database backups are provided by the hosting platform. Application state is reproducible from the container image and the committed migrations, both of which are verified on every pipeline run.

> **Limitation.** The provider's schedule and retention have not been confirmed in writing, and no restore has been attempted from this system's backups.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:packages/db/drizzle` — Committed migrations reproduce the schema from empty.

### IA-2 — Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)

**Status:** Partial · **Responsibility:** system

Accounts authenticate with an email address and password and receive a signed bearer token. Token validation pins the algorithm to HS256 and checks the issuer, so a token presented under a different algorithm, or minted by another service, is rejected rather than trusted.

> **Limitation.** Tokens are stateless, so an issued token stays valid for its full lifetime. Nothing -- a password change, an account deletion, or known compromise -- can invalidate one before it expires.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/auth/jwt.ts` — jwt.verify with an algorithm allowlist and issuer check.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/__tests__/auth-hardening.test.ts` — Rejects unsigned, algorithm-confused, foreign-issuer, expired and forged tokens.

### IA-5 — Authenticator Management

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** system

No usable default signing key exists anywhere in the source tree. Production requires a supplied secret of at least 32 bytes that is not one of the placeholders published in the repository; outside production an ephemeral key is generated per boot. Orchestration files take secrets as required external inputs and refuse to start without them.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/env.ts` — resolveJwtSecret enforces presence, length and non-placeholder.
- `evergreen:docker-compose.yml` — ${JWT_SECRET:?} and ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?} are required inputs.
- `evergreen:.security/secret-allowlist.json` — Declared exceptions to secret scanning, each with a written reason.

### IA-5(1) — Password-Based Authentication

**Status:** Partial · **Responsibility:** system

Passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes at work factor 12, the value OWASP recommends. Length and format are enforced by a shared schema used by both the API and the client. Failed authentication is answered in time that does not depend on whether the account exists, so login cannot be used to enumerate registered users.

> **Limitation.** Credentials created before the work factor was raised keep verifying at the old, weaker cost, and bcrypt silently ignores anything past the first 72 bytes of a password the schema allows to be 128 characters long.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/auth/hasher.ts` — BCRYPT_ROUNDS = 12, with the range validated at construction.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/auth/jwt.ts` — Decoy-hash comparison on the unknown-account path.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/__tests__/auth-hardening.test.ts` — Counts comparisons to prove both paths do equal work.

### IR-4 — Incident Handling

**Status:** Partial · **Responsibility:** shared

The audit trail provides the source material for handling an incident: structured events, correlation ids linking client-visible errors to server-side causes, and pseudonymous account ids that allow an affected account to be traced without exposing addresses.

> **Limitation.** There is no alerting, no on-call rotation and no exercised response procedure. Detection today depends on somebody reading the logs.

**Evidence**

### RA-5 — Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** system

Three layers run on every pull request and weekly: the dependency closure that actually ships is audited and gates the build at high severity; the built image is scanned for vulnerable operating-system and language packages; and the Dockerfile and compose file are scanned for misconfiguration. Closure resolution is exact, so advisories in the mobile toolchain are reported without blocking a service that does not contain that code.

> **Limitation.** Scanning is in place, but the mobile toolchain currently carries open advisories that cannot be cleared without a major framework upgrade.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:scripts/dependency_audit.py` — Resolves the production closure from the lockfile.
- `evergreen:.github/workflows/security.yml` — Trivy image and config scanning, both failing the build.

### SA-11 — Developer Testing and Evaluation

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** system

95 automated tests, of which 47 cover security behaviour specifically: configuration refusal paths, response headers, cross-origin policy, rate limiting, body limits, audit content, and token validation. Database behaviour is exercised against a real PostgreSQL instance in CI rather than only against in-memory doubles.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/__tests__/security.test.ts` — 23 tests covering request-handling controls.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/__tests__/postgres.integration.test.ts` — Transaction and constraint behaviour against a real database.

### SA-15 — Development Process, Standards and Tools

**Status:** Partial · **Responsibility:** system

Security gates are part of the pipeline rather than a separate review step, and the same gates run locally through `npm run security`. Workflows declare least-privilege permissions and do not persist checkout credentials.

> **Limitation.** Action references still resolve by mutable tag. Anyone able to move a tag changes what runs in the pipeline, with access to the workflow token.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:.github/workflows/ci.yml` — Least-privilege permissions, persist-credentials false.
- `evergreen:scripts/pin_actions.py` — Rewrites tag references to commit SHAs; --check runs offline.

### SC-13 — Cryptographic Protection

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** system

Only reviewed primitives from maintained libraries are used: bcrypt for password storage, HMAC-SHA256 for token signatures with the algorithm pinned at verification, and SHA-256 for audit pseudonymisation. No cryptography is implemented in this codebase.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/auth/hasher.ts` — bcrypt behind a PasswordHasher interface.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/auth/jwt.ts` — HS256 pinned on both sign and verify.

### SC-18 — Mobile Code

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** system

The API returns JSON only, so its Content-Security-Policy forbids loading anything at all and denies framing, alongside nosniff, no-referrer and cross-origin isolation headers. Responses default to no-store so per-user data is not cached by intermediaries.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/security/headers.ts` — Policy written out explicitly so it is auditable without reading a dependency.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/__tests__/security.test.ts` — Asserts each header on real responses.

### SC-28 — Protection of Information at Rest

**Status:** Partial · **Responsibility:** shared

Credentials are stored only as bcrypt hashes and are never returned by any endpoint, which a test asserts. Volume and disk encryption are provided by the hosting platform.

> **Limitation.** Behavioural entries and email addresses are stored in plaintext columns. Field-level encryption has not been implemented and provider disk encryption has not been confirmed in writing.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:packages/db/src/schema.ts` — password_hash column; no plaintext credential is stored.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/auth/jwt.ts` — toPublicUser strips the hash from every response.

### SC-5 — Denial-of-Service Protection

**Status:** Partial · **Responsibility:** shared

Request bodies are bounded, general and credential traffic are rate limited in separate buckets, and the container has memory and process limits so a runaway loop cannot exhaust the host. Liveness probes are deliberately exempt from throttling.

> **Limitation.** Per-process counters do not hold across replicas, and volumetric protection at the network edge is the provider's.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/app.ts` — bodyLimit and two rate-limit buckets.
- `evergreen:docker-compose.yml` — memory and pids limits.

### SC-8 — Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity

**Status:** Inherited · **Responsibility:** provider

TLS termination is performed by the hosting platform. The application asserts HSTS in production so a browser will not downgrade to plaintext, and refuses to accept a plaintext http CORS origin in production.

> **Limitation.** Cipher suites, certificate issuance and renewal are the provider's and must be confirmed against the provider's own attestation.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/security/headers.ts` — HSTS emitted only when NODE_ENV=production.

### SI-10 — Information Input Validation

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** system

Request bodies are validated against zod schemas shared between the API and the client, so both agree on what is acceptable. Validation failures return a stable machine-readable code with per-field detail, which the client localises. Database constraints back the application checks rather than relying on them alone.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/routes/validate.ts` — parseBody rejects anything the schema does not accept.
- `evergreen:packages/core/src/schemas/auth.ts` — Shared schemas are the single definition of valid input.
- `evergreen:apps/api/src/__tests__/postgres.integration.test.ts` — Asserts the unique-email constraint holds at the database.

### SI-11 — Error Handling

**Status:** Implemented · **Responsibility:** system

Unhandled errors return a generic body and a correlation id; the detail stays server-side. Errors carry stable machine-readable codes that the client maps to localised messages, so raw server text is never rendered in the interface.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/app.ts` — onError returns a generic body and logs detail server-side.
- `evergreen:packages/core/src/errors.ts` — Closed set of client-facing error codes.

### SI-4 — System Monitoring

**Status:** Planned · **Responsibility:** shared

The data a monitoring capability needs is produced -- structured security events with outcomes, pseudonymous subjects and correlation ids -- but nothing consumes it yet.

> **Limitation.** No collection, no detection rules, no alerting. Events are written to stdout and, beyond whatever the platform retains, go unread.

**Evidence**

- `evergreen:apps/api/src/security/audit.ts` — The event stream a monitoring capability would consume.
